title: The Sketch Law: low-dose LoRA-DPO as a random sketch of one data-determined function, and the rank and dose at which seed-invariance breaks
central_question: Is the function learned by standard-recipe LoRA-DPO (lr 5e-6, 1 epoch, PEFT default init B=0 / A kaiming, TRL trainer with peft_config) a seed-independent functional of (base, data, program) that each unseeded lora_A merely sketches -- dW = B*A0 ~ -sum_t lr_t * adam(G_t A0^T) A0, a Johnson-Lindenstrauss estimator of ONE data-determined gradient direction in function space, orthogonal in weight space by construction -- so that (i) cross-run weight cosines carry no mechanistic information unless A0 is shared, (ii) function space is the only valid space for 'same solution' claims, and (iii) the invariance breaks predictably when rank falls below the preference gradient's effective rank k_eff, or when the trajectory leaves the first-order regime (reward-margin saturation at high dose, F5c), with A-displacement explicitly ruled out as the regime variable because Probe 2 shows lora_A frozen even at 40x lr and 3 epochs?
hypothesis: At the paper recipe A stays within ~2% of its unseeded kaiming init (sum-of-lr bound: sum lr ~1.6e-4 vs element scale ~0.009), and data order is seeded identically (SeedableRandomSampler from seed 42 applied AFTER the PEFT wrap), so each seed's adapter is an independent random sketch of the SAME data-determined gradient G. Falsifiable consequences: (a) seeded twins (seed set before get_peft_model) share lora_A bitwise and reach per-layer dW cosine > 0.9, the residual being kernel nondeterminism; (b) different-seed adapters have weight cosine ~1/sqrt(r*fan_in) ~ 0.004 yet per-token logit-delta cosine > 0.8 and disattenuated per-task profile r >= 0.9 (the reliability ceiling F5b already shows for three 4090 retrains), on both raw and typing-forgiven metrics, and across the 4090 and 5080 stacks; (c) freezing A reproduces gain and profile; (d) the rank-32 concatenation average of two orthogonal adapters preserves the gain although ||dW||_F falls by 1/sqrt(2) (sketch averaging is variance reduction, not basin averaging, refuting magnitude primacy in this regime); (e) between-seed profile agreement declines monotonically with rank below k_eff (working form r_seed ~ 1/(1 + k_eff/r); the r=16 ceiling implies k_eff <~ 2); (f) left (output-side) top-k singular subspaces of dW are shared across seeds while right (input-side) subspaces sit at chance, reconciling Hu et al. Sec. 7.2 with F3; (g) a second adapter at the positive-control recipe (lr 2e-4 x 3 epochs, margins ~11) does NOT reproduce the first's per-task profile (disattenuated r < 0.8), whereas early-stopped high-lr runs (train accuracy < 0.9 at stop) agree with each other and with the low-lr consensus -- predictive multiplicity is a signature of margin saturation, not of step size or of A moving; (h) any TRL-based LoRA run that reports a seed has an init the seed never reached, detectable in released adapters.

(F3 is unclaimed)' and its link to LoRA Without Regret's capacity argument. trace-vs-pair-data-efficiency OPEN: Nikolich et al.'s cross-objective LoRA cosines (SFT/RFT >= 0.97, DPO near-orthogonal) have no seed-variance floor. silent-hardware-faults (2/5) OPEN: 'nothing certifies that a low-rank dW is in the equivalence class of legitimate outcomes' -- a seed-invariant function class is that certificate (feeds Gap 4). What exists: lazy-A theory ('The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics'), frozen/random-A results ('Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models', 'VeRA', 'HydraLoRA'), random-subspace intrinsic dimension ('Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning'), benign-landscape theory ('LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima', 'LoRA Training Provably Converges to a Low-Rank Global Minimum or It Fails Loudly'), thin-shell regularity ('Model Stock'), location consistency for full-FT RL ('Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models', 'The Path Not Taken') -- all for SFT/vision/full-FT, none measuring function-space agreement of seed-orthogonal LoRA-DPO adapters or its breakdown with rank or dose. Nobody has (a) a second seed in the rich regime to show multiplicity returning, (b) the averaging test, (c) function-space cosine next to weight-space orthogonality, (d) the Hu 7.2 left/right resolution, (e) a frozen-A arm under DPO, or (f) an audit of released TRL adapters. The project's head start is unique: Probe 1 already answered the map's open profile question at zero compute (disattenuated r 1.06/1.08/1.06; 1.12/1.13/1.11 typing-forgiven), Probe 2 measured A-drift and matched the predicted 0.0039 against the measured 0.0042, and both boundary cases are banked (F5: original adapter r = -0.10, reliability 0.21/0.52; F5c: poscontrol r 0.43-0.56, SD 33pp vs 16pp, margins 11 vs 0.78).
predictions: Zero-compute sketch signature: a random-projection simulation of all 224 module shapes reproduces the recorded per-layer dW cosine 0.0042 +/- 0.0044 ONLY when B_i = G*A0_i^T with a shared G (independent random B gives mean ~0; the recorded mean is ~14 SE above zero), and splits by module: q/k/v/o/gate/up (fan_in 4096) ~0.0039 vs down_proj (fan_in 14336) ~0.0021 under 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) (1.9x smaller) versus ~3.5x smaller under r/d_in -- the simulation plus the per-module compare_adapters.py output adjudicates the scaling. Hu-style top-k subspace similarity phi(k=1..4) on the RIGHT side is at chance (< 0.05). REFUTED if independent-B simulation already yields the positive mean, if down_proj cosines are not smaller, or if real retrains share right-side top directions (restores Hu Sec. 7.2 and kills the pure lazy-A account).

Seeded twins (same seed set before get_peft_model): lora_A 224/224 bitwise identical (poscontrol/init_vs_training.py); per-layer dW cosine >= 0.9; profile r at the reliability ceiling. REFUTED if dW cosine < 0.5 -- kernel nondeterminism alone would then decorrelate weights (Summers-Dinneen regime), not the random A0.

Different-seed pair (s1, s2; lr 5e-6 x 1 epoch; same 5080 session): weight-space dW cosine 0.004 +/- 0.005 but per-position logit-delta cosine on the 31 ruler prompts >= 0.8 (>= 0.5 minimum), disattenuated per-task profile r >= 0.9 on raw AND aggregate_if_typing_imported, both arms >= +7pp vs the interleaved null and within 3pp of each other; cross-stack class membership: raw r >= 0.8 with the 4090 retrain consensus (the same six tasks ace_oss_11023/17851/4327/24748/23069/23132 gain >= +25pp, ace_oss_3243 loses >= 10pp, typing NameErrors ~2 per 155). REFUTED if logit-delta cosine < 0.3 while profiles still agree (identity would then not be first-order), if profile r < 0.7 (F5b does not transfer to this stack), or if cross-stack r < 0.5 (function stack-dependent; F1 must be re-read as a stack effect rather than a fault).

Frozen-A arm (lora_A.requires_grad=False, same seed as a trained-A twin): aggregate within the 15-replicate MDE (~4pp) of the trained-A twin; disattenuated typing-forgiven profile r >= 0.9; compare_adapters.py cosine ~1 (shared A0). REFUTED if frozen-A loses >= 5pp or r < 0.7 (A's small drift carries function).

Rank-32 concatenation average of the two different-seed adapters ([A1;A2], [B1/2, B2/2]): ||dW||_F ~ 0.71x a parent, yet aggregate gain within +/-2pp of the parents' mean (e.g., parents +9pp, average >= +7pp) and profile r with each parent >= 0.9. REFUTED (magnitude primacy / random-subspace energy view, Model Stock center-approximation) if the average's gain <= 0.75x the parents' or recovers only after sqrt(2) rescaling.

Rank sweep at alpha/r = 2, lr = 5e-6*sqrt(16/r), two seeds per rank: between-seed disattenuated profile r falls monotonically with rank; with the r=16 ceiling implying k_eff <= ~2, predict r=4 in 0.7-0.9 and r=1 in 0.35-0.7. Weight-space corollary on the same adapters: principal angles between col(B_seed1) and col(B_seed2) (left singular subspaces of dW) are small for the shared k_eff directions while row spaces (span of A0) are orthogonal; output-side top-4 subspace similarity exceeds input-side similarity by >= 5x per module, and the weight-space k_eff estimate agrees with the behavioral one within a factor of 2. REFUTED if r=1 twins still agree >= 0.9 on the typing-forgiven profile (a global attractor, not a sketch), if col(B) subspaces are also mutually orthogonal, or if right-side similarity is high (A aligned to data, contradicting Probe 2). If both sides are at chance (~r/d), G's effective rank exceeds r -- also informative.

Regime boundary: a second unseeded lr 2e-4 x 3-epoch adapter vs the existing dpo_adapter_poscontrol, same session: mean gain +11 +/- 4pp but disattenuated per-task r <= 0.7 (split-half reliabilities >= 0.85), per-task delta SD ~30pp, opposite sign on >= 5 tasks that swing more than 30pp, typing fails ~0.1/row. Early-stopped high-lr arms (lr 2e-4, --max-steps 17, two seeds; train accuracy < 0.9, margins < 2 at stop) agree with each other at the ceiling AND correlate >= 0.8 (disattenuated) with the low-lr consensus, with larger per-task SD. REFUTED if the two poscontrol seeds agree >= 0.9 (a deterministic second lr-indexed attractor; multiplicity absent in both regimes), if early-stopped seeds disagree with each other (step size, not saturation, breaks invariance), or if they agree with each other but not with the low-lr profile (lr selects a different deterministic function).

Optional dose-response: an lr 2e-5 x 1-epoch adapter has disattenuated r with the low-lr consensus between 0.8 and 0.95 and per-task SD between 17 and 33pp, i.e. profile agreement declines monotonically with sum(lr). Zero-compute companion: the three retrain logs' loss/margin trajectories coincide to 2-3 decimals across seeds while training_poscontrol.log saturates (accuracy 1.0 from epoch ~1.7, margins 10-11); the saturation step is the predicted onset of seed-dependence, testable by checkpoint-level fingerprints.
A displacement at the original recipe ||A_T - A_0||_F / ||A_0||_F < 0.02 in all 224 layers (measurable only with seeded A0). REFUTED if > 0.10 in any attention layer.

theoretical_payoff: Establishes (or refutes) that conventional-learning-rate LoRA post-training is sketch-and-readout / random-feature regression on a frozen unseeded projection: the map (data, program) -> FUNCTION is deterministic while (data, program) -> WEIGHTS is a random orthogonal family. Consequences: (i) seed-invariance of the learned function is guaranteed once r exceeds k_eff, independent of init, so the behavioral agreement-vs-rank curve is an estimator of the intrinsic rank of the preference signal -- unifying LoRA Without Regret's ~1 bit/episode capacity argument, Aghajanyan's intrinsic dimension, Hu et al.'s shared top directions (a left-side / A-training artifact) and Mukherjee/Zhu's location-consistent full-FT RL updates (the consistent object is G, which LoRA sketches) under one mechanism; (ii) weight-space similarity of adapters is the wrong instrument (cos ~ 1/sqrt(r*fan_in) is a tautology) and function space the right one, so Nikolich et al.'s cross-objective cosines need a seed floor and Model Stock's thin shell is reached at its 90-degree extreme; (iii) predictive multiplicity (Marx; McCoy; D'Amour; Jordan) is NOT a universal property of fine-tuning but a signature of leaving the first-order regime (reward-margin saturation), with A-displacement ruled out -- the first regime boundary for underspecification in post-training; (iv) soups of orthogonal adapters are variance reduction, not basin averaging, and magnitude primacy fails in this regime; (v) every TRL-based LoRA-DPO/SFT/GRPO paper that reports seeds has an init the seed never reached -- a one-line upstreamable fix, and an adapter reproducible as (seed, B) at half the size (VeRA-like); (vi) reproducibility and attestation of LoRA post-training must be certified in function space, supplying the calibrated, replica-free, seed-free functional acceptance test that the silent-corruption and ZK-attestation literatures lack (Gap 4 builds on it). Matters to LoRA/PEFT theorists, model-merging work, RL-with-LoRA practitioners, anyone reporting single-seed or 'seed variance' of TRL LoRA runs, and training-integrity researchers.
risks: Stack transfer: the 4090 retrains (torch 2.6/cu124, py3.11) vs this RTX 5080 (torch 2.11/cu128, py3.12, bnb 0.50.1); the different-seed pair is itself a replication and may fail for stack reasons unrelated to the theory -- the within-session frozen-vs-trained and twin contrasts are primary, the cross-stack comparison secondary; a local r=16 twin pair removes the confound.

Frozen-A and seeding require wrapping the model yourself before DPOTrainer; trl 0.12.2 must accept a pre-wrapped PeftModel (it checks is_peft_model) and prepare_model_for_kbit_training is currently called twice -- validate on a --max-steps 1 smoke run first.

Adam's per-coordinate normalization and DPO's nonlinearity in B distort the linear sketch scaling; the exact 1/(1+k/r) form may fail while the monotone-in-rank ordering survives -- preregister the qualitative ordering as primary. The sketch model also predicts seed noise ~1/sqrt(r*m) with m ~224 (~2% at r=16, ~7% at r=1), below the instrument's reliability floor, so the rank sweep may not discriminate; the averaging test and the saturation boundary are the discriminating experiments, and the averaging test assumes first-order linearity at ||dW||_F ~0.02/layer.

n=15 replicates per arm gives an aggregate MDE of ~4pp and per-task profiles at 75 draws/task (rep3-level split-half ~0.69), so disattenuated correlations carry CIs of roughly +/-0.2; bootstrap CIs are mandatory; low-rank arms with smaller gains may be underpowered (mitigated by lr ~ 1/sqrt(r) compensation and pooling seeds); 20 rounds (+80 min) if a session allows.

Profile agreement may be dominated by the shared typing-import behavior (F2 NEW, 51-58% of the gain); all correlations must be reported on aggregate_if_typing_imported as well (Probe 1 shows identity holds there too), and if Gap 2's typing-ablated corpus is available the rank sweep should be repeated on it.
peft's alpha/r scaling confounds rank with effective lr; hold alpha/r = 2 (not the default alpha=32).

GGUF export of a rank-32 merged adapter via the Ollama ADAPTER path is untested; export_adapter.py's acceptance checks must pass before the arm is scored, and the served-Q4 vs PEFT-fp16 discrepancy (heldin_history not_the_served_artifact) adds instrument noise to the function-space vs behavior comparison; a norm-matched random-B null arm may degrade generation, so include a 0.5x-scaled variant.

Kernel nondeterminism on the 5080 (no determinism flags set) may leave seeded twins with dW cosine well below 1; that residual is itself the measured kernel term of the variance decomposition, but if large it weakens the 'A0 is the only unseeded draw' story.

TDR is unmitigated on this machine (no admin, TdrDelay unset), so every training run carries the F4 risk; a silently corrupted run would itself be an out-of-class adapter and could be misread as theory failure -- the step-1 liveness assert and Adam-bound gate are partial detectors; re-run once before concluding.

The lab PC wipes on logoff; adapters (168 MB each) are gitignored, so seeds + lora_B (+ 84 MB GGUF) must be pushed every session or the weight-space half is lost again (as happened with the 4090 adapters). Session A is ~2.9 h of a 4-h window; drop to 12 rounds rather than skip the push.

title: Compliance before competence: offline DPO amplifies an environment-conditional verifier regularity from a minority of contrast pairs into the majority of a measured gain, and construct-valid gain is what survives a verifier-environment swap
central_question: When the oracle's error is a deterministic function of the verification environment rather than a stochastic flip -- the pinned Python 3.11 verifier raises NameError on un-imported typing annotations that Python >= 3.14 accepts, and the AceCode prompts carry annotated signatures -- and the same verifier both labels the preference pairs and scores the benchmark, does offline DPO learn that instrument component first, faster and out of proportion to its share of the contrast pairs (a simplicity bias toward the lowest-description-length separating feature), so that a measured gain decomposes into an instrument-compliance term that saturates at low dose and a competence term that is overwritten at high dose -- and can construct-valid gain be defined operationally as the part invariant under perturbation of the verifier environment (re-scoring fixed weights and retained generations under Python 3.14), with no optimization pressure against the verifier at all?
hypothesis: DPO on binary execution verdicts allocates its update first to the cheapest chosen-vs-rejected discriminator; for this corpus that is 'emit from typing import' (a single early-token decision that flips a NameError). Therefore (i) pairs whose rejected half fails ONLY by a typing NameError are a minority (5-30% of the 918; the 13 seed prompts carry no annotations, so the annotations were model-introduced) yet all three retrains learn the import to near-saturation (typing fails 11 -> 2 per 155 generations) and 51-58% of each +10pp is attributable to it: amplification ratio (behavior share / contrast share) >= 2; (ii) along the training trajectory the implicit-reward margin on typing-class pairs saturates before logic-error-class pairs; (iii) the learned behavior is a saturating (step) function of typing-pair dose, not proportional; (iv) removing or neutralizing typing contrasts (against a size-matched random-drop control) removes the typing behavior and leaves the +3 to +6pp residual on the same two tasks (ace_oss_17851, ace_oss_24748), and that residual does not track per-task test weakness; (v) label-swapping reverses it; (vi) amplification is monotone in update magnitude (poscontrol: 0.1 typing fails/row, typing-forgiven gain +2.0pp); (vii) re-scoring the SAME generations under a Python 3.14 verifier removes the typing component and leaves the residual. Consequently the robustness results for stochastic verifier noise (1/(1-2 eps) penalties; tolerance to 15-40% flips) do not transfer to execution verifiers, whose systematic error is anti-robust because it is learnable: the relevant quantity is not the verifier's FP rate but the learnability (contrast consistency, description length) of its error.

theoretical_payoff: Replaces the stationary-noise picture of imperfect verifiers with a learnability picture: DPO's margin gradient is steepest along the cheapest edit that flips the most rejected halves, so a systematic, environment-conditional failure cause is learned first, amplified far beyond its corpus share and saturated before the construct-relevant signal -- structured, one-sided, learnable verdict 'noise' that neither the stationary-noise RL theory (Cai et al.) nor symmetric-flip DPO theory (rDPO; Gao et al.) describes, and whose relevant quantity is the learnability of the verifier's error, not its FP rate. It is the deflationary dual of reward hacking: the model learns the instrument rather than the task with zero optimization against the verifier, supplying the offline-propagation measurement and the zero-pressure base rate that the verifier-hacking literature (Ray; Rajan; MBPP-Honeypot) leaves open and the first offline-regime answer to Rajan's causal test. It makes the psychometric instrument/construct distinction operational for RLVR: construct-valid gain = gain invariant under verifier-environment perturbation (change the instrument's environment, hold the weights fixed), with the instrument term's share growing with dose (F5c's collapse from +11.4 to +2.0pp) -- a counterfactual re-verification protocol that turns 'instrument integrity' from a taxonomy into a measurable share of any reported gain, and a reporting standard for every code-DPO/RLVR paper whose benchmark prompts carry typing annotations (AceCoder, PLUM, CodeDPO, Sol-Ver). Readers would have to re-examine 'An Imperfect Verifier is Good Enough' (15% tolerance holds for unstructured noise; structured noise is learned, not tolerated), 'Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable yet Noisy Rewards' (the channel is not stationary), 'Spurious Rewards' (Llama3 does not gain from random rewards but does from systematic instrument-correlated rewards -- the gain is signal-driven, the signal is about the verifier), and 'Code-R1' (false positives 'confuse the model'; systematic false negatives teach it). Matters to code-RLVR/DPO authors (what a +10pp on an execution benchmark means), verifier-noise theorists (a structured non-stationary task-correlated noise model), reward-hacking researchers, benchmark metrologists (the harness as a calibrated instrument), and the F6 instrument-integrity taxonomy (interpreter-version ground truth becomes a measured term).
risks: aggregate_if_typing_imported is an UPPER-BOUND counterfactual (a failure whose only error is a typing NameError counts as a pass, not a re-execution); the decisive number must come from the dual-verifier re-execution, which requires retained completions that no past eval kept and a harness change.

If the corpus census finds almost no typing-contrast pairs (the 13 seed prompts are bare, un-annotated functions), the mechanism shifts to a style correlate (likelihood displacement per Razin, or same-base subliminal transfer per Cloud et al.), the ablation arm becomes uninformative and the design must change -- the zero-compute count must be done first.

Ablating typing pairs shrinks the corpus and changes data order and step count; the size-matched random-drop control is mandatory and the import-neutralized variant (same pairs, neutralized contrast) is the cleaner primary ablation; the typing-only corpus may be tens of pairs, so scaling epochs to 57 steps risks overfitting (compare to a size-matched random subset if p < 10%). Chosen halves may import typing for unrelated reasons, blurring the dose estimate; report both 'rejected typing-only' and 'chosen imports typing' doses.

title: Block-scale capture: blockwise 8-bit Adam stops being Adam in the 256-element quantization block that holds Llama-3-8B's massive-activation channel, and an Adam-displacement invariant detects it without a replica
central_question: Are the ~170 elements of layers.1.mlp.down_proj.lora_A that exceed the exact-Adam worst-case displacement bound (3.16 x sum(lr) = 0.0547) by up to 3x -- all inside the 256-aligned column window [2304,2559], which contains intermediate channel 2427 that Probe 4 measured as a prompt-invariant massive activation (max|x| 386.5 vs median 0.013, 30,000x), while lora_A everywhere else stays inside its kaiming init box -- produced by bitsandbytes' blockwise (blocksize 256) 8-bit quantization of Adam's second-moment state being dominated by that one channel, so that the recorded optimizer ('adamw_bnb_8bit') silently applies a non-Adam update rule to the channel's 255 block-neighbours in every run on this model; is the effect deterministic and model-conditioned rather than data- or seed-conditioned; is it functionally material; and can the per-tensor bound |delta theta| <= 3.16 x sum(lr_t) -- which holds for exact Adam regardless of seed, data order or kernel nondeterminism -- serve as a free, replica-free training-time integrity invariant that separates optimizer artifacts from benign nondeterminism and from hardware faults (F4)?
hypothesis: dL/dA[:, j] scales with the input activation x_j, so channel 2427's 30,000x activation makes its gradient second moment set the 256-element block's absmax; the 255 neighbours' v underflow in the 8-bit dynamic format, their effective step sizes explode past the Adam bound, while 2427's own entries (the absmax holder) stay accurate -- exactly Probe 4's signature (column 2427 itself NOT an outlier at 0.0044; neighbours up to 0.175, 21x the init bound; 93 columns x all 16 rank rows). With identical seed and data order the excess vanishes under 32-bit optimizer states (adamw_torch, or adamw_bnb_8bit with min_8bit_size raised above the 229,376-element tensor) and reappears under adamw_bnb_8bit and paged_adamw_8bit, localized to the same block regardless of seed or corpus; it recurs at every learning rate relative to sum(lr); and it is either functionally measurable or demonstrably immaterial (Probe 4 predicts immaterial for this adapter: the block holds 70.4% of layer-1 down_proj's ||dW||_F^2 but 0.94% of the whole adapter's, and the layer's activation-weighted output delta is ~entirely channel 2427's contribution because the neighbours' activations are ~0.013) -- in both cases 'adamw_bnb_8bit' is a well-formed recorded config value that does not describe the applied update (the candidate 7th F6 measurement-integrity failure), and the displacement bound plus a step-1 A-invariance check is a closed-form post-hoc detector needing no replica, no determinism and no recomputation.

title: What 'the update took' means under nondeterminism: a functional acceptance class calibrated on healthy seeds, a norm-matched random-adapter null, and a fault-type taxonomy separable in function space
central_question: Given that the legitimate outcomes of an unseeded LoRA-DPO procedure are weight-orthogonal adapters with one function (F5b), is 'the update took' definable only as membership in that functional outcome class -- and do corruption phenotypes separate in function space by fault type: omission faults (lost steps) producing a scaled-down copy of the legitimate function, commission faults (wrong gradient values: partial GEMM, kernel abort with resubmission, the 8-bit optimizer-block anomaly) producing an uncorrelated direction at preserved norm -- such that the original F1 'null' adapter (same norm, zero mean, profile uncorrelated with the healthy class at r = -0.10, split-half reliability 0.21/0.52) is classifiable as commission/random and indistinguishable from a norm-matched random LoRA, and such that a single cheap observation of a new adapter (no replica, no seed, no generation) can accept or reject it?
hypothesis: In the lazy LoRA regime the procedure's legitimate outcome class is a single function sampled with instrument noise, so a replica-free, seed-free acceptance test exists: the function-space fingerprint (per-position logit-delta direction on a fixed probe set, or the per-task delta profile) of a healthy run lies within the between-seed dispersion of healthy retrains, while (a) a norm-matched random LoRA (kaiming A, Gaussian B with per-layer ||B||_F or ||B A0||_F matched to a healthy adapter, built on the healthy adapter's own A0), (b) a commission-fault run, and (c) the F1 adapter fall outside it with |cos| < 0.2 and a zero-mean per-task redistribution of low reliability that nonetheless passes an effect-variation test (so F5's permutation criterion alone cannot distinguish trained-null from noise); omission-fault runs stay inside it (cos > 0.8) with proportionally reduced gain; structural integrity checks (per-layer norm, rank, Adam bound) pass for random and commission arms alike and therefore cannot make these distinctions.

theoretical_payoff: Would establish that for a nondeterministic training procedure the only coherent notion of 'the update took' is membership in its functional outcome class -- which in the lazy LoRA regime is a single function -- and that corruption phenotypes are separable in function space by fault type (omission -> scaled-down copy; commission -> uncorrelated direction at preserved norm, indistinguishable from a norm-matched random adapter). This gives the SDC / training-integrity literature the replica-free, seed-free functional oracle it says it lacks (Ma et al. need a shadow replica; Altenbernd needs seeded recomputation; SDCHunter needs replay), defines integrity-as-effect as distinct from integrity-as-structure (Shang et al.'s drift proofs, VeriLoRA), supplies the missing null model for 'noise-like' adapters (Ilharco's random-vector control re-aimed at an improvement claim, with Neural Thickets / NoisyTune as the alternative it tests against), and imports effect-variation tests (Ding-Feller-Miratrix, Crump et al., PERMANOVA) into LLM evaluation as the statistics that distinguish a no-op from a redistributing adapter -- and shows those statistics alone cannot distinguish a redistributing adapter from noise, which the reliability/correlation criterion can. It reframes Hochlehnert-style replication failures: a null can be a corrupted instrument rather than evaluation variance, and F1 is classified without invoking TDR. Matters to training-integrity and attestation researchers, reproducibility methodologists, consumer-GPU practitioners with no ECC or replica, and the heterogeneous-effects statistics line.
risks: Fault models are software simulations; they test separability of phenotypes, not that a Windows TDR event produces either one (vendor docs say a TDR leaves the CUDA context reporting errors, so the silent path is still unexplained); a real TdrDelay manipulation needs admin this machine lacks.

The original F1 adapter's weights are not on this machine; its classification rests on behavioral rows only (forged-rep and ctl-his with same-session nulls are present; only 5 of the original 40 null rows are), so the zero-compute classification is behavioral, not weight-space.

Norm-matching must match both the per-layer norm and the kaiming A structure (or reuse the healthy A0) so the random arm is not trivially distinguishable by spectral signature (intruder dimensions) rather than by function; a full-norm random adapter may degrade generation, hence the 0.5x variant.

Function-space fingerprints are computed on the bnb-4bit PEFT path while behavior is measured on the Q4 GGUF ADAPTER path; a served-vs-PEFT discrepancy could blur the acceptance threshold -- heldin_history's single not_the_served_artifact check should be repeated for each arm.
Calibrating the acceptance threshold needs >= 3 healthy seeds (a third is +25 min); with only two, the healthy dispersion is a single number.

Commission-fault severity (p=0.2) is a guess; if too mild the arm lands inside the healthy class and the taxonomy appears to fail -- the severity sweep adds 50 min of training and three fingerprints but no extra eval if only fingerprints are used.
